verdicts.quote: Any invalid row or file-level problem means no user is created
a list of every invalid row with its row number, the column, the value found and the reason.
`Ann@X.com` in the file, when `ann@x.com` already exists (or occurs in an earlier row), is reported "already registered" (or "duplicate of row N").

the message lists each unrecognised header exactly as found in the file (for example `email;name` for a semicolon-separated file, or `role`, or `password`) … Imported users get the default non-admin role and importing cannot make admins
verdicts.missing: The file cannot assign roles. The specification gives no rule for checking a requested role against the particular importer's authority.

verdicts.quote: A signed-in account that is not currently an active admin is refused
verdicts.missing: The admin requirement is explicit. Its relationship to permission to create a user individually is unspecified.

verdicts.quote: The first record is the header and columns are matched by name, in any order … whose header lacks `email` or has unknown, duplicate or empty column names. They see that nothing was created
A leading UTF-8 byte-order mark is ignored … Fields are separated by commas and records end at LF or CRLF; a field wrapped in double quotes may contain commas and line breaks
First-access messages are sent only after the import has been fully applied … A rejected or failed import sends no message to any address in the file
one of 1,048,577 bytes is rejected with HTTP status 413 and a message stating the 1,048,576-byte limit; no user is created.
A zero-byte file or a file with only blank records is rejected … A file with a header but no data rows is rejected … A fully valid file creates exactly one user per data row
A second submission of a file already applied is rejected with every data row reported as "already registered" and the user listing unchanged.
small enough to finish synchronously … an in-progress indication is shown until the result arrives.
verdicts.missing: The admin receives the synchronous result. The specification gives no background import workflow or way to learn of completion after leaving the page.

verdicts.quote: an applied import sends one per created user, which may arrive after the result page is shown.
verdicts.missing: Whether invitations go out together or in batches, and what sending rate applies.

verdicts.quote: Each imported user goes through the same first-access step (an invitation, a set-password message or whatever an individually created user goes through; unconfirmed what that is) … the file contains no password
verdicts.missing: First access follows individual creation. The account's initial active or pending status and whether it already has a password are unspecified.

verdicts.quote: After the response is sent, the file's contents are not stored anywhere readable by admins or operators, other than the users it created.
For each attempt the operator can find, in the product's logs, the admin's identity, the time, the file's name, the outcome (created, rejected rows, rejected file, refused, failed)
After a timeout or dropped connection during processing the file is either fully applied or not at all … After a rejection the admin corrects the file and submits it again
verdicts.missing: Whether an admin can deliberately cancel a running import or select only the failed rows for retry, and how either action would work.

verdicts.quote: A file at the maximum size completes within 30 seconds … After the admin presses submit, the control is disabled and an in-progress indication is shown until the result arrives.

Every action and every outcome of single-user creation, including its fields, validation and first-access messages, is the same with the feature present as without it. … The import does not change, deactivate or delete existing users
An email longer than 254 characters is invalid … A name longer than 200 characters is invalid … Values echoed in the report are shown as plain text
verdicts.missing: How formula-like values echoed in results would be kept from executing when opened in a spreadsheet.
